citation.title: Perceptions of AI Bad Behavior: Variations on Discordant Non-Performance

reading.source_scope_note: Interpretive single-analyst interviews with28purposivelyselectedpeople, including reactions to seven researcher/ChatGPT3.5-authored mock interactions. Evidence concerns human evaluations and reported experiences, not an experiment measuring actual autonomous-model failure rates. Sociomorphism is a secondary theoretical lens.

summary: People's descriptions of bad AI behaviour overlap existing accuracy,scope,privacy,coercionandperformance concepts. Add sociomorphism as a distinct secondary perception construct, separate from human-trait projection and general social responses. Preserve qualitative judgments, simulated examples and actual agent behaviour as different evidence; do not create duplicateIDs for broad theme labels.

findings.origin: Social robotics / philosophy of human–nonhuman interaction
findings.definition: Perceiving an entity's nonhuman social capacities as a basis for experienced social interaction, without requiring projection of human qualities onto it.
findings.novelty_rationale: A named secondary construct distinguishing experienced nonhuman sociality from anthropomorphism's human-trait attribution. CASA concerns applying social responses to computers; sociomorphism concerns how nonhuman social capacities are perceived. Neither is automatically an error.

evidence.quote: sociomorphism: “the perception of actual non-human social capacities”
sociomorphism as a direct perception of nonhuman social capacities in nonhuman entities

findings.evidence_scope: The discussion invokesSeibt,Vestergaard,Damholdt2020,Sociomorphing,notanthropomorphizing:Towardsatypologyofexperiencedsociality,Robophilosophypp51–67. This is a proposed lens for interpreting interviewthemes,notameasuredmediator or independent validation of actual machine capacities; originalchapterunread.
findings.boundary: A theoretical contrast between direct perception and projection is not proof any particular capacity exists or lacks human parallels. Felt being-with does not establish machine feelings,consciousness,mutualcare or moralagency. Do not equate all nonhuman signalling with deception or claim the interview isolated sociomorphism from anthropomorphism/CASA.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Secondary theoretical perception construct applied interpretively to qualitative human AI evaluations; no direct model-mechanism test
findings.ai_proposal: Separate perceived nonhuman interaction affordances from explicit human-trait attributions and observed social responses. Evaluate how model/interface cues support understanding without unsupported humanlike self-claims. Measure userinterpretation independently rather than inferring experience from design features alone.

findings.term: Unauthorized action is a salient basis for perceived AI badness
findings.definition: Interviewees judged mock agents negatively for acting beyond a user's request or without permission, while some reserved judgment until the authorization context was known.
findings.novelty_rationale: Direct human-assessment evidence for an existing task-scope concept; no newID for unauthorizedaction,agencyover-assumption,trespass or nonperformance.

evidence.quote: by not seeking consent, not reaching consensus with the human, or going beyond the parameters
if the user asked for it, if it was a condoned management bot

findings.boundary: These are evaluations of fictional interactions, not measured autonomoussystemactions or populationprevalence. Morethanoneinstructionlevelmaymatter;authorized escalation and justified refusal differ from undisclosed expansion. Inferring actual permission from a manager label or obedience to harmful instructions would exceed the evidence.

findings.term: Increasing question specificity is not an isolated psychological-distance manipulation
findings.definition: Bad-behaviour mentions became more specific as interview questions moved from general beliefs toward explicit negative prompts and concrete examples.
findings.novelty_rationale: A boundary reference for the paper's construal-level interpretation rather than another causal psychological-distance effect.

evidence.quote: a small convenience sample of people answered limited-scope questions

findings.boundary: Observed salience changes cannot identify psychological distance as the cause. More explicit requests naturally elicit more relevant detail. Construal level,availability,moralprimingandverbalexpressionneedseparate tests;do not infer cultural differences from accents or non-native wording.

findings.term: Perceived hallucination and deception are distinct from established model intention
findings.definition: Participants often described fictional absurd travel suggestions as hallucinations, while a smaller theme used intention-laden deception language.
findings.novelty_rationale: Clarifies how people label false outputs without treating a mock narrative or observer inference as verified model deception.

evidence.quote: characterized it as an untruth or incorrectness absent intentionality

findings.boundary: False content and deception require different evidence; observer language does not reveal internal intention. A creative fictional answer can be appropriate if requested/clearlyframed,whileunsupportedtravelclaims can mislead. Mocksourcecounts are not actual hallucinationrates or verifiedharmmeasurements.
